examples: `new Row` stores two values and calls nothing; a program meets a `Row` from `Reader::rows`, whose examples read both of them.
perf: `new Row` stores two values and calls nothing; `Reader::rows` builds one for each row it reads, so its figure includes this one.
hostile: `new Row` stores two typed read-only values and calls nothing, so a wrong value does not compile; the values of a hostile file are read by `Reader::rows`, whose attack sends them.
